courses.name: Bash
courses.blurb: The language of the terminal. Variables, tests, loops and pipelines that glue other programs together.

courses.name: brainFOOD
courses.blurb: A row of boxes, a pointer and eight symbols. Tiny, strange and surprisingly powerful.

courses.name: C
courses.blurb: The small language under operating systems and most other languages. Types, loops and functions.

courses.name: C#
courses.blurb: Microsoft's main language: properties, records, pattern matching, LINQ queries and async code.

courses.name: C++
courses.blurb: C with classes grown up: references, the standard library, RAII and modern C++20.

courses.name: Chisel
courses.blurb: A hardware construction language in Scala. The program builds a circuit; it does not step through one.

courses.name: Classic BASIC
courses.blurb: Numbered lines, PRINT and GOTO: the BASIC that home computers of the late 1970s and 1980s switched on into.

courses.name: COBOL
courses.blurb: Records, money and plain-English statements. Still runs payments and payroll at banks, insurers and government agencies.

courses.name: Delphi
courses.blurb: Current Object Pascal: Unicode strings, generics, records with methods and anonymous methods, for Windows, macOS, Linux and phones.

courses.name: Delphi 5/6/7
courses.blurb: Object Pascal with drag-and-drop forms. Fast to build real Windows programs.

courses.name: Fortran
courses.blurb: The first high-level language, now modern and array-friendly. Still behind weather models, physics codes and fast maths libraries.

courses.name: Go
courses.blurb: A small language for services and tools. One looping keyword, and slices instead of a pile of collection types.

courses.name: HTML and CSS
courses.blurb: The two languages every web page is made of: HTML for what each part is, CSS for how it looks. Each example has a live preview.

courses.name: INTERCAL
courses.blurb: The first joke language: politeness is mandatory and numbers come out in Roman numerals.

courses.name: Java
courses.blurb: Classes, strong types and a huge standard library. Runs bank systems, Android apps and countless university courses.

courses.name: JavaScript
courses.blurb: The language every web browser runs, and with Node.js, servers and tools too. Modern syntax, closures, classes and async.

courses.name: Kotlin
courses.blurb: Google's preferred language for Android apps. Null safety, data classes, lambdas and far less typing than Java.

courses.name: LOLCODE
courses.blurb: A real, working language written in lolcat speak. HAI to KTHXBYE.

courses.name: Malbolge
courses.blurb: Built to be nearly impossible to program, and it rewrites itself as it runs.

courses.name: Numerical methods
courses.blurb: How computers find roots, areas and solutions when there is no formula. Each method explained, then built and tested in several languages.

courses.name: Perl
courses.blurb: Sigils, regular expressions and hashes. The glue language of log files, CGI scripts and system tools.

courses.name: PHP
courses.blurb: The server-side language behind a large share of websites. Echo a page, handle forms and print safe HTML.

courses.name: Piet
courses.blurb: Programs are pictures. Colour changes between blocks are the instructions.

courses.name: Python
courses.blurb: A friendly, readable language used everywhere from web servers to science. The full beginner course.

courses.name: QuickBASIC
courses.blurb: Microsoft's structured BASIC with a full-screen editor. Where many people wrote their first game.

courses.name: Rust
courses.blurb: A modern systems language. The compiler keeps track of who owns each value.

courses.name: Slick
courses.blurb: Pascal Costanza's s-expression notation for Go. Same language underneath, Lisp-shaped on the page.

courses.name: SQL
courses.blurb: Ask questions of a database: SELECT, filtering, grouping, joins and changes, on a small sample database.

courses.name: Swift
courses.blurb: Apple's language for apps on every Apple device. Optionals, structs, enums with values, and closures.

courses.name: Turbo Pascal
courses.blurb: Borland's fast, friendly Pascal with the blue IDE. Where structured programming was learned for a decade.

courses.name: TypeScript
courses.blurb: JavaScript with types checked before it runs. Interfaces, unions, generics and typed async code.

courses.name: Visual Basic .NET
courses.blurb: The BASIC of the .NET platform: English-like blocks, Option Strict, classes, LINQ queries and the whole .NET library.

courses.name: Whitespace
courses.blurb: Only spaces, tabs and newlines mean anything. Everything you can see is a comment.

courses.name: Win16
courses.blurb: C and the 16-bit Windows API: WinMain, the message loop and window procedures.

courses.name: Z80 Assembly
courses.blurb: Talk to the processor directly: registers, flags, loops and the stack.
